terms.definition: The primary AI agent in planner-service, powered by the Anthropic Claude LLM, that conducts a structured conversational dialogue with the user to extract a BusinessModel and generate SolutionHypotheses. The Planning Agent orchestrates the SpecialistNavigator and PatternMatchingService.

A domain-specific AI sub-agent (Form, PDF, Comment, or Notification Service) that the Planning Agent delegates to for deep technical guidance when a particular ADSP service is identified as relevant in a SolutionHypothesis. Each Specialist Agent is a separate Nx microservice.

A structured JSON representation of a user's business problem, composed of typed BusinessConcept entities (Actor, Goal, Activity, Decision, etc.), their relationships, assumptions, and a confidence score. The Business Model is iteratively refined through conversation with the Planning Agent.

A proposed composition of ADSP services and implementation order, generated by the Planning Agent when the BusinessModel reaches sufficient completeness (confidence score >= 70 per BR-004). A SolutionHypothesis has a defined lifecycle: draft, proposed, accepted, rejected, or superseded.

A configurable template that describes a known GoA business process type (e.g., Case Management, Grant Application). Stored in the ADSP Configuration Service under a tenant-scoped namespace. Patterns include domain language, signals, ADSP service mappings, and clarifying questions to guide the Planning Agent.

The internal Planning Agent component responsible for determining which Specialist Agent (if any) is applicable given the current SolutionHypothesis and user context, and for delegating the conversation to that specialist via its integration stub.

The internal service within planner-service that computes a composite confidence score for each BusinessPattern against the current BusinessModel, using domain language overlap, strong signal presence, and concept type distribution. A pattern is surfaced to the Planning Agent only when the score meets or exceeds 60 per BR-005.

An atomic unit of a BusinessModel, classified by conceptType (e.g., Actor, Goal, Activity, Decision, Document). The Planning Agent extracts and classifies concepts from the user's natural language descriptions. A concept's type drives the confidence score calculation and pattern matching.

The persistent top-level record representing one user's engagement with the planner-service. A session contains all ConversationMessages, the BusinessModel, and all SolutionHypotheses. Sessions are scoped to a tenantId and userId, and have a lifecycle status (active, paused, completed, archived).

Alberta Digital Service Platform — the GoA's shared platform for building and operating digital services. ADSP provides common services including Keycloak for authentication, MongoDB for data persistence, RabbitMQ for event messaging, and the Configuration Service for tenant-scoped settings.

Tenant Management Webapp — the existing ADSP web application used by GoA program areas to manage their ADSP tenant settings. planner-service embeds its React UI into TMW as a routed section, sharing TMW's authentication flow and GoA Design System theme.

The ADSP SDK function called at planner-service startup to register the service with the ADSP platform, enabling Keycloak JWT validation, Configuration Service access, domain event type registration with the event service, and platform health endpoint discovery.

A numeric value on a 0-100 scale representing how complete the Planning Agent considers the current BusinessModel to be. Calculated from concept classification completeness, presence of Actor and Goal concepts, and proportion of Unknown-typed concepts. A score of 70 or above triggers automatic SolutionHypothesis generation per BR-004.

An immutable record of a significant state change in planner-service (e.g., session-created, hypothesis-generated) published to the ADSP event service via RabbitMQ. Each event includes tenantId, sessionId, and a typed payload. Only the six event types registered with the ADSP event service at startup are permitted per BR-012.

A placeholder implementation of an integration point (INT-001 through INT-008) used during development and testing when the live external service is not available. Stubs implement either fail-closed (returns a service-unavailable error), lookup-empty (returns an empty valid response), or fire-and-forget (silently discards the request) behavior.
